body.p: Applicant submits this Amendment and Response to address the non-final Office Action dated October 23, 2024 ("Office Action"). Claims 1 and 6 have been amended without intending to abandon or to dedicate to the public any patentable subject matter. Claims 2 and 7 were previously canceled. Claims 3 and 8 have been canceled herein without intending to abandon or to dedicate to the public any patentable subject matter. No claims have been added. No new matter has been added as a result of these amendments. Therefore, claims 1, 4-6, and 9-11 are present for examination. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended.
In the Office Action, the Examiner objected to claims 3 and 8 due to their dependencies

upon canceled claims. Claims 3 and 8 have been canceled herein without intending to abandon or to dedicate to the public any patentable subject matter. Accordingly, the objection to claims 3 and 8 is rendered moot.

Claims 1, 3-6, and 8-11 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2016/0114726 to Nagata et al. ("Nagata") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2019/0061740 to Ohira et al. ("Ohira") and U.S. Patent Publication No. 2009/0254249 to Ghoneim ("Ghoneim").
Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw the rejections made under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for at least the following reasons.
The Cited References Fail to Teach Several Features as Claimed

When determining whether a claim is obvious under 35 U.S.C. § 103, an examiner must make "a searching comparison of the claimed invention - including all its limitations - with the teaching of the prior art." In re Ochiai, 71 F.3d 1565, 1572 (Fed. Cir. 1995) (emphasis added). Thus, "obviousness requires a suggestion of all limitations in a claim." CFMT, Inc. v. Yieldup Intern. Corp., 349 F.3d 1333, 1342 (Fed. Cir. 2003) (citing In re Royka, 490 F.2d 981, 985 (CCPA 1974) (holding that to establish prima facie obviousness of a claimed invention, all the

claim features must be taught or suggested by the prior art)). Applicant respectfully submits that several features in the pending claims are neither taught nor suggested, either expressly or inherently, in any of the cited references. For at least the reasons below, Applicant submits that the rejections of the claims should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended. Among other things, Nagata, Ohira, and Ghoneim, whether viewed separately or in combination, fail to at least teach, suggest, or disclose the combination of features of "comparing a suspension dam ping of a rear axle of the vehicle with a predetermined suspension dam ping when the vehicle is performing the reverse parking maneuver" and "under the condition that the suspension dam ping~ of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension dam ping, a second control signal is output to cause the suspension dam ping~ of the rear axle to increase, wherein the second control signal is associated with the first control signal," as recited in amended independent claim 1.

Firstly, in constructing the rejection on pending claim 1, Office A ction asserts that the following disclosure of Ghoneim teaches the claimed features of "comparing a suspension damping of a rear axle of the vehicle with a predetermined suspension damping" and "under the condition that the suspension damping of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, a second control signal is output to cause the suspension damping of the rear axle to increase" (See, e.g., Office Action, p. 6):
"When the vehicle is moving slowly (e.g., when maneuvering into
or out of a parking box), it may be appropriate to have a stiffer
setting of the suspension system than when travelling at a normal speed for urban or overland traffic. Therefore, the controller may also be adapted to distinguish between a high forward speed state
of motion and a low (including negative) forward speed state of
motion and to set a higher stiess of the suspension system in the
high forward speed state than in the low forward speed state."
Applicant respectfully disagrees with this assertion.
The instant application provides a vehicle control method that specifically aims to
enhance the safety and comfort of a vehicle during reverse parking maneuvers. One of the key objectives of the instant application is to mitigate the impact and potential body tilting that

occurs when a vehicle reverses into a parking space and collides with parking stops or other obstacles. This is achieved by adjusting the damping characteristics of the rear axle suspension and the reversing speed. Especially, if the actual damping is found to be lower than the predetermined value, the system automatically outputs a control signal to increase the damping. This adjustment helps to absorb the shock and reduce the body tilting that may occur when a vehicle collides with parking stops or other obstacles.
Applicant respectfully submits that Ghoneim provides no teaching or suggestion

whatsoever regarding the adjustment of suspension damping to prevent impact and body tilting that may occur when a vehicle reverses into a parking space and collides with parking stops or other obstacles.
Specifically, Ghoneim is primarily concerned with a suspension control system that

adapts the stiffness of the suspension system based on the vehicle's current state of motion. The system is designed to provide improved maneuverability when cornering or in transient states by adjusting the stiffness to one of several discrete values depending on the driving conditions.

It should be noted that, stiffness refers to the suspension's resistance to deformation, which affects the vehicle's stability and handling. By contrast, damping refers to the ability of the suspension to dissipate the energy from impacts and oscillations, which directly affects how the vehicle responds to bumps and collisions. Stiffness and damping are distinct parameters that should be adjusted independently to optimize ride comfort and handling stability.

In this connection, Ghoneim pays no attention to the adjustment of suspension damping, and at best teaches the adjustment of suspension stiffness when a vehicle reverses into a parking space for better handling stability. Further, while Ghoneim provides a comprehensive approach to adjusting the stiffness of the suspension system based on various driving conditions, it fails to discuss the specific problems of shock and body tilting that can occur when a vehicle collides with parking stops or other obstacles, much less address such issues. Therefore, on the basis of Ghoneim's disclosure, one of ordinary skill in the art would not be motivated or inspired to derive the insight to regulate suspension damping when the vehicle is performing the reverse parking maneuver, let alone arriving at the solution of "comparing a suspension damping of a rear axle of the vehicle with a predetermined suspension damping" and "under the condition that the suspension damping of the rear axle is lower than the predetermined suspension damping, a
second control signal is output to cause the suspension damping of the rear axle to increase." as currently claimed.

Secondly, in constructing the rejection on pending claim 1, the Office Action asserts that the following disclosure of Ghoneim teaches the claimed feature "the second control signal is associated with the first control signal" (See, e.g., Office Action, p. 8):
"Based on a comparison of the vehicle velocity v with a very low threshold vstopth, a stop index vstin is set to 1 (S25), indicating
that the vehicle is moving, or to 0 (S26), indicating that is
practically standing still. If it is determined that the vehicle is
moving, its speed v is compared to another threshold vlowth
amounting to a few kilometer per hour. If the threshold is
exceeded, indicating that the vehicle is moving in a normal traffic
flow, the index vlo_in is set to 0 (S28). If v is below vlowth it is
likely that the vehicle is carrying out a difficult maneuver such as
moving into and out of a park box, and vlo_in is set to 1 (S29)."
Applicant respectfully disagrees with this assertion.

As described in paragraph [0034] of the instant application, "the above second control signal may be associated with the above first control signal, that is, determinations of the first and second control signals are coordinatively considered, allowing the adjustment of the speed and the adjustment of the suspension damping of the rear axle to be coordinated, thereby providing a comfortable riding experience for a driver and passengers in the vehicle. For example, a set of braking force adjustment coefficient and damping adjustment coefficient are obtained by table look-up according to a current speed and a current suspension damping, and an original braking force adjustment controlled quantity and an original damping adjustment controlled quantity are optimized (e.g., multiplied) by these two coefficients, respectively."

According to the solution recited in the currently amended claims, and with reference to paragraph [0034] above, the adjustment of the suspension damping of the rear axle is coordinated with the adjustment of the reversing speed. Among other things, this coordination is a novel aspect that enhances the safety and comfort of the vehicle during reverse parking maneuvers by reducing the impact and body tilting that can occur when the vehicle collides with parking stops or other obstacles.
Applicant respectfully submits that Ghoneim fails to at least teach or suggest the

coordination of suspension damping adjustments with vehicle speed adjustments as provided by the pending claims. Ghoneim teaches a method of comparing the vehicle's current speed with various thresholds (e.g., vstopth, vlowth) to determine the vehicle's current state of motion (e.g., moving, standing still), and then adjusting the suspension stiffness to match the determined state of motion. The focus of Ghoneim is solely on the adjustment of the suspension stiffness, without any mention of speed adjustment, let alone coordinating the adjustment of the vehicle's speed and the suspension damping.
For at least the foregoing reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that none of the cited references teach, disclose, or suggest the combination of features recited in the amended independent claims.
In addition to being dependent from an allowable independent claim, the dependent claims provide further reasons for allowance.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
For at least the reasons set forth above, Applicant submits that the rejections of the claims should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Applicant does not acquiesce to any objection, rejection, or argument not specifically addressed herein. Rather, Applicant believes the amendments and arguments contained herein overcome all objections, rejections, or arguments.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant believes that all pending claims are in condition for allowance and such disposition is respectfully requested. In the event that a telephone conversation would further prosecution and/or expedite allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned.

The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge to Deposit Account No. 19-1970 any fees under 37 CFR §§ 1.16 and 1.17 that may be required by this paper and to credit any overpayment to that Account. If any extension of time is required in connection with the filing of this paper and has not been separately requested, such extension is hereby Petitioned.
Respectfully submitted, SHERIDAN ROSS P.C.
